traditional_joinery_review.status: CAPACITY HOLD — historical straight feet and a default-only flared-foot geometric proposal
traditional_joinery_review.scope: The section measurements and existing-joint findings below use the saved baseline. The default top-entry variant has the separate foot proposal described here.
traditional_joinery_review.existing_joint: Horizontal radial tie end into the side of a cupola upright; the lower well stays open.
traditional_joinery_review.traditional_candidate: Through wedged half-dovetail tie-to-post joint, with a separate hardwood wedge and bearing housing where required.
traditional_joinery_review.geometric_limit: A head retaining the full 10-inch tie depth reaches the current post bottom, leaving no timber below that head. A smaller head or reversed flare is an unverified adaptation, not a resolved repair.
traditional_joinery_review.kingpost_distinction: A traditional suspended kingpost can hang a continuous tie from a vertical through tenon. That arrangement is different from these radial tie ends entering cupola posts; the cupola and ring forces must be resolved before selecting the joint.
release_requirements: Resolve cupola/ring/tie forces and bearing support
Size cheeks, tenon, housing, remaining timber and any peg or wedge from the actual loads and material
Verify insertion, access and retention through the complete assembly sequence
traditional_joinery_review.provenance_limit: The references document joint families in other structures. They do not establish the concealed joinery of the Bluetime building or approve dimensions for this model.

default_top_entry_proposal.joint: Bottom-entry housed dovetail with a 3 by 8 inch neck, 4 inch head width, 4 inch engagement, 1:8 side flare and a separate 3/4 inch transverse wooden peg.
default_top_entry_proposal.assembly_scope: Local matching-solid and withdrawal tests pass. Full-scene sequencing is certified separately against the exact disassembly manifest; this report does not certify that route.
default_top_entry_proposal.design_hold: The one-inch minimum post cheeks, peg, bearing, neck, splitting resistance and ring/tie forces require structural design from actual loads and material.
default_top_entry_proposal.source_scope: Documents the joint family only, not this foot orientation, dimensions or load capacity.

findings.title: Center connection capacity remains unresolved
findings.finding: The saved baseline and historical perimeter variant retain straight lower-foot tongues without positive withdrawal restraint. The default top-entry variant now has actual flared feet, exact matching bottom-entry cavities and removable wooden pegs. Their nominal geometry passes, but the one-inch minimum receiving-post cheeks are not structurally qualified.
findings.action: Resolve neck, cheek, bearing, peg, splitting and block-shear demands from the cupola/ring/tie forces. The default foot is an adaptation of a documented housed-dovetail family, not verified hidden joinery from the reference building. Do not assume the polygon or plywood alone supplies ring action.

findings.title: Main-rafter tongue exceeds the receiver-based proportion
findings.finding: The generic width rule uses the 8-inch rafter: 8/3 = 2.667 inches. In a 6-inch receiving post, nominal cheeks are only (6 - 2.667)/2 = 1.667 inches before neighboring cuts. TFEC 1-2019 §§3.4.10–11 use the receiving member and require each cheek at least the mortise width for the prescribed tension-joint provisions.
findings.action: Redesign this joint from the receiving post and load demand. A broader head is not a remedy for thin cheeks. A dovetail is a different connection requiring its own neck, bearing and splitting/block-shear checks.

findings.title: Two-inch insertion is not a ready-made pegged tension joint
findings.parts: Unchanged generic two-inch shoulder tenons in the saved baseline
findings.finding: No peg location or end distance is modeled. For illustration, the TFEC full geometry factor calls for 4D loaded-end distance in a softwood tension member: a 3/4-inch peg alone needs 3 inches from peg center to the loaded end. The current two-inch tongue cannot provide that distance.
findings.action: Resolve species, peg diameter, receiving-face edge distances and joint arrangement together; do not simply drill the existing tongues. This comparison does not assign a capacity or prohibit every alternative tested detail.

findings.title: Outer seats carry gravity but do not lock against uplift
findings.finding: R0 bears across the 8 × 8 post head (64 in² nominal horizontal footprint). Each short rafter has approximately 12 in² of horizontal bearing on its ring beam. These are real support surfaces, not merely the colored cavity edge seen in the screenshot. No rated uplift or sliding restraint is modeled.
findings.action: Keep broad gravity bearing; check heel/block shear, remaining rafter section and the signed force direction. Retain or adjust the seat only after those checks. Add a designed restraint for force reversal; a deeper notch alone is not a solution.

findings.title: Braces, eave-ring joints and post bases need a complete lateral system
findings.finding: All 24 main braces now use full 2 by 6 inch stock, matching one-inch face housings and 48 physical half-inch wooden pegs. Local withdrawal and fit checks pass; their bearing, peg and reduced-section capacities remain unverified. Eave-ring joints share post heads with other cuts. Foundation hardware is a geometric proposal, and enclosed-wall sheathing and attachments are not designed.
findings.action: Trace wall/roof shear through collectors, braces or shear panels, post joints and foundations. Check both wind directions, load reversal, combined notches and erection stability.

findings.title: Cupola ceiling and roof require attachments
findings.finding: The horizontal half-inch plywood and eight exposed horizontal ceiling spokes now follow the user-confirmed arrangement. Ceiling spoke 4 × 6 sizes and roof-rafter 2 × 6 depths are assumptions. Center miters touch but do not themselves resist separation. Finish boards are not assigned an invented thickness.
findings.action: Design center and perimeter connections plus plywood grade, panel joints, edge blocking and fastening. Do not credit the plywood as a diaphragm until its complete boundary load path is specified.

findings.title: Earlier prototype is not verified stronger
findings.finding: The earlier model used algorithmic keys and larger-looking interlocks. Its own engineering review recorded severely reduced webs and unresolved raising/tool access. Those shapes were not a verified traditional joinery schedule.
findings.action: Retain useful viewing features and compare real housings/shoulders, but do not restore arbitrary keys as a structural fix.

findings.title: Nominal cavity fit passes independent checks
findings.parts: All modeled recesses and mating timber solids
findings.finding: The actual removed-stock cavities pass independent occupancy and section checks at the recorded numerical tolerances. All timber pair overlaps, registered contacts and connected-solid checks also pass. The former residual meshes were numerical artifacts and are no longer exported or displayed.
findings.action: Read the hash-bound cavity-fit audit for methods and tolerances. Geometry agreement does not establish connection strength, shrinkage allowance, tool access or a complete raising sequence.

load_coefficients.usage: For a uniform pressure q in lb/ft² of horizontal projection, total vertical force equals q times plan area. Per-bay values apply only to a symmetric load accounting case, not individual joint reactions. Actual wind/snow are not assumed uniform or divided equally. Timber weight equals volume times confirmed density. No load magnitudes or capacities have been assigned.
